placeholder.description: The symbol that stands for these words in protectedText.

protectedText.description: The passage as it would go out: each symbol where its words stood; the passage itself when protection is off.

isRead.description: False until Singularity has read the document; it then has no passages.

protectedName.description: The document's name as the line above its passages carries it.

withheld.description: Papinian Guard could not mask it, so no request would send it.

passageCount.description: Every passage the document has; more than passages holds when it is long.

archivedAt.description: When it was archived; empty while it is open.

archivedBy.description: Who archived it, by actor id; empty while it is open.

protectionLoading.description: The protection model is still loading after launch: not ready yet, and not a problem either.

keptHere.description: Why this chat's work stays on this computer, when it does: then primaryModel is the local model it really runs on (null when nothing here can run it) and destination is local, whatever AI Setup would choose.

keptHereMessage.description: Why it stays here, or the sentence a send stops with when nothing here can run it.

downloadedBytes.description: While a package managed by Singularity downloads or installs: how many of its downloadBytes have arrived.

canInstallHere.description: The protection model can be installed on this computer now from a Debug build's developer copy (localModels.sync with this model's id). Always false in a Release build.

OutboundCall.description: One real call that sent something off this device, recorded when it was made. Markers are the placeholders that stood in what was sent, never the values behind them.

url.description: The public page address a web_open call sent.

symbolScope.description: An opaque id of the protection table the call's markers were numbered by: markers name values only within one table, and one operation can hold calls of several.

pictures.description: The pictures a member attached that the call carried as they are, unmasked: each by its name, size and SHA-256, never its bytes.

OutboundRecord.description: What left this device for one operation (a chat turn's taskId), read from every Routing Log run it wrote.

callsRecorded.description: False for a request written before calls were recorded: only its route, protection and counts are known.

operationType.description: The work behind the operation, from its task when known: matter_task (a chat turn), context_automation, memory_keeping; empty when not known.

protectedEntityIds.description: For a record whose markers were not kept, every Project entity id a marker stood in for in its requests; null unless that list is whole.

phase.description: Only while status is loading: the warm-up's real current step. starting = choosing where it runs and verifying the installed package; loading_model = opening the model; preparing = re-verifying the opened package and running the first protection pass.

elapsedMs.description: Only while status is loading: milliseconds since this warm-up began (0 before it has begun).

expectedMs.description: Only while status is loading: how long the last finished warm-up of this model version took on this computer; null when none has finished here yet.

recovery.description: The one action that moves protection forward, or null when there is only waiting: install_here (a Debug build's developer copy, localModels.sync papinian-ner), sign_in (signing in to Legal Machines gives this computer its download session; account.signIn), retry_download (localModels.sync papinian-ner), retry_load (localModels.load papinian-ner).

doneBytes.description: While the package downloads, is checked or installed: how many of its bytes have arrived.

totalBytes.description: With doneBytes: the package's whole size in bytes.

progressPercent.description: Only while downloading: doneBytes of totalBytes, 0-99.

outbound.description: What left this device for the Project's latest operations, newest first (at most 200), from the one outbound record: the Routing Log, completed by the Project's own tasks (a Context update or memory upkeep that wrote no entry, a web search an entry missed). Null when that record cannot be read.

outboundTruncated.description: True when older operations were left out of outbound: an entity not found in it may still have left in one of them.

DisclosedSegment.description: One run of a passage: words that left as written, or a hidden value. In the sent form a hidden run's text is the marker exactly as it left; beside the local text it is the original words, read on this device.

sentAs.description: The marker exactly as it left ("[[E4]]", "[[E4.last]]"); only on a hidden run.

marker.description: Its base marker, which names its DisclosedValue; only on a hidden run.

label.description: The value's readable label ("Person 2"); only on a hidden run.

category.description: The value's kind; only on a hidden run.

DisclosedValue.description: One value a protected request hid: what the provider received instead (sentAs), a readable label numbered by kind in the order the operation first sent it, the Project entity it belongs to, and the original words as the Project's own text has them - read now, never from a kept restoration mapping.

entityName.description: The linked Project entity's own name, from the local Entity Registry.

originals.description: Each way the value is written where a passage lined up with its local text; empty when none did.

missing.description: Why no original is shown when none is and the Project names no entity for it: the text it came from has changed since, cannot be read now, does not line up word for word, or it left in a part of the request Singularity does not keep word for word. Null otherwise.

DisclosedPassage.description: One passage of an operation's protected requests exactly as it left (cut from the payload that was sent), read beside the Project's text now.

reading.description: aligned: every hidden value has its original. ambiguous: the words line up but the hidden values cannot be told apart. changed: the local text is no longer the text it was sent from. unaligned: the sent form does not line up with its own text. unavailable: no local text could be read. Only aligned carries local.

documentChanged.description: The document has changed since; an aligned local text is how the passage read when it was sent.

calls.description: The requests that carried the passage in this form.

PassageDisclosure.description: What a protected request of one operation sent for one cited passage. recorded: the passage is among what left; not_kept: the operation's passages are kept but not this one; unavailable: the operation's passages are kept, but this passage's text cannot be read now to find it among them; not_recorded: the operation keeps no record of its passages.

formCount.description: How many different forms of this passage left; passage is the latest.

OperationDisclosure.description: What one operation's protected requests sent: every value hidden and what replaced it, the lawyer's instruction and each document passage as they left, every relation Singularity worked out on this device and sent, and - under the protected computation protocol - the role lines and table blocks the requests carried and every operation the model asked Singularity to work out.

recorded.description: False when the operation keeps no record of its passages: hidden then names only what its calls record.

relations.description: Each relation the operation's requests carried: the line the model saw, and the same line read with its originals on this device (null when a value was not kept or cannot be worked out again).

withheldRelations.description: How many relations Singularity worked out but kept on this device under the relation policy.

roles.description: Each role line the requests carried, once: what the model was told a symbol is, in the material's own words.

tables.description: Each spreadsheet table block the requests carried, once.

operations.description: Every operation the model asked Singularity to work out on this device, in the order asked, refused and failed ones included.

DisclosedRelation.description: One relation Singularity worked out on this device over protected values and sent with a request. Never a value kept: local is re-derived when asked.

sent.description: The line exactly as it left: symbols and closed words.

DisclosedRole.description: One role line a request carried. Never a value kept: local is read again with the originals when asked.

sent.description: The line exactly as it left: symbols and the material's own words.

DisclosedTable.description: One spreadsheet table block a request carried.

sent.description: The block exactly as it left.

why.description: The model's reason, when it asked for a sheet the evidence did not touch.

DisclosedOperation.description: One operation the model asked Singularity to work out on this device and what it was sent back. Symbols, codes and closed words; local is re-derived when asked, never kept.

requested.description: The operation as the model asked it.

returned.description: The line exactly as it was sent back, or null when none was.

local.description: What it worked out, with the originals, read on this device; null when there is no result or a value cannot be read again.

observation.description: Whether the model learned a relation from it.

build.description: Which build this is, as a design partner's problem report says it.

recorded.description: Whether this computer's work record holds the call.

confirmation.description: What the provider's own record says the call cost, or null before it is asked.

change.description: A document change's full description; for web.search and web.open, { outbound: { kind, destination, leaves, query?, jurisdiction?, allowedDomains?, url? } } - exactly what leaves this device if the step is allowed.

liveAnswer.description: The answer as far as the model has written it, while this process runs the operation; null otherwise. Display only, never persisted.

citations.description: The Project sources a proposed change rests on, while it waits for approval; empty otherwise.

asking.description: The question the running operation is parked on, while it waits for the lawyer's answer; null otherwise.

questions.description: Every question this operation has put to the lawyer, in the order asked, with its answer once given.

ChatQuestion.description: One question the model put to the lawyer, as Singularity normalized it: Singularity assigns the ids and always lets the lawyer answer in their own words.

ChatQuestionAnswers.description: The lawyer's answers keyed by question id: the options they chose and anything they wrote in their own words.

ChatAsking.description: The question set a running operation waits on. Its id is the only thing chat.answerQuestion accepts as questionId.

ChatQuestionRecord.description: A question set as the operation keeps it. answers is null while it is open, when the lawyer left the decision to Singularity, and when it was never answered; a record nothing waits on any more reads unanswered.

number.description: The number the answer cites it by; 0 for a source the answer was written from without citing it inline (ChatConversation.cpp).

questions.description: The questions this turn put to the lawyer, in the order asked; one still open when the turn finished reads unanswered.

artifactTitle.description: Present only for a generic ProfessionalArtifactAction result (create_content/append_content/replace_content/update_cells); null for DirectDocumentWork/AdvancedWorkflow, which keep their own existing specialized presentation (directDocumentWorkTitle, professionalReview) instead.

artifactFormat.description: The real physical format of the affected artifact (e.g. docx, xlsx, csv, txt, markdown, json, xml, html) - present only alongside artifactTitle.

artifactChangeKind.description: The real, backend-decided outcome - never guessed frontend-side from resultingVersion.

change.description: The change as written, when the task kept it - so the chat shows it the way the document now does.

viewer.description: Who is looking and what they may do, the same viewer organisation.get holds.

ArtifactChange.description: A change to a Project document as a person reads one - before approving it and again after it was written: what kind, the text that goes, the text that comes, and rows with the columns they fit when rows go into a table.

operations.description: An edit's steps, each where the document says it (kind edit only).

DocumentView.description: A Project document as its author laid it out, read fresh from its current file (matter.readDocumentView). Change marks are against comparedToVersion; 0 means nothing was compared and every mark is "unknown".

page.description: null when undeclared or not a Word document.

footer.description: The body section's default footer; fields read as their cached result.

workbook.description: xlsx, csv and tsv only (blocks is then []); null for every other format and for a workbook that could not be read.

listMarker.description: The number or bullet Word draws, counted from numbering.xml ("1.1", "(a)", "ARTICLE II", "•"); "" when not in a list.

indentFirstLineTwips.description: Negative for a hanging indent. Paragraph > list level > style chain > document defaults; null where nothing declares one.

spacingAfterTwips.description: Paragraph > style chain > document defaults; null where nothing declares one.

isTitle.description: Written in the Title style or a style based on it.

revision.description: The paragraph itself inserted or deleted (its paragraph mark's revision).

formatRevision.description: The paragraph written differently in a tracked change (w:pPrChange: another style, alignment, spacing, indentation or numbering); kind "formatted". null where its look is its own.

DocumentViewRun.description: A stretch of text written one way. Deleted runs (revision.kind "deleted") are the file's struck words and are not part of what the paragraph says.

formatRevision.description: The run written differently in a tracked change (w:rPrChange); kind "formatted". The run's marks are how it is written now. null where its look is its own, and on a run a tracked insertion or deletion holds.

noteId.description: The referenced note's id in DocumentView.notes ("footnote-<w:id>" / "endnote-<w:id>"); "" on every other run.

noteNumber.description: The number Word draws for the reference; 0 on every other run.

commentIds.description: Comments whose range covers this run; an empty-text run carries a comment anchored at a point.

link.description: External hyperlink target (w:hyperlink r:id or a HYPERLINK field); "" otherwise.

pageBreak.description: A w:br w:type="page" run, with empty text.

DocumentViewRevision.description: One of the Word document's own tracked changes (w:ins/w:moveTo inserted, w:del/w:moveFrom deleted, w:rPrChange/w:pPrChange/w:tcPrChange formatted), by whom and when, as the document writes them. date is w:date as written - Word has long written its local clock there with a "Z" - and "" where the document gives none; dateUtc is Word's own UTC stamp (w16du:dateUtc), "" where the document gives none. changes says what a formatting change did in plain words ("bold", "not italic", "14 pt", "aligned center"); empty for an insertion or deletion. For a formatting change, wasRun is a run's marks as they stood before it and wasAlignment a paragraph's alignment as it stood ("" = the reader's default) - what the page drawn with every change rejected shows; null where the change did not move them, and for an insertion or deletion.

tableId.description: The locator's own table id ("table-<n>", nested tables counted where they stand); "" outside the body.

hasBorders.description: Any non-nil edge in tblBorders, directly or through the table style chain.

revision.description: The row itself inserted or deleted in a tracked change (w:trPr/w:ins, w:trPr/w:del).

rowSpan.description: Rows a vertical merge's anchor covers, itself included; 1 otherwise.

blocks.description: The cell's whole content in order, nested tables included.

DocumentViewPage.description: The last section's page size and margins, in twips.

DocumentViewNote.description: A footnote or endnote the body refers to, numbered in reference order (separators excluded).

DocumentViewComment.description: A Word comment, in the order its mark stands in the document; date is ISO 8601 as written, "" where absent.

DocumentViewWorkbook.description: A spreadsheet (xlsx, csv, tsv) as its workbook. A CSV or TSV is one sheet named after its file, header row included, with no styles.

DocumentViewSheet.description: One sheet, in workbook order. rowCount/columnCount are the used extent (0 for an empty sheet); widths are characters, heights points; every index is 0-based and every range inclusive.

rows.description: Sorted by index; only rows the sheet actually has.

removedCells.description: Cells comparedToVersion showed something in that this sheet no longer has.

DocumentViewSheetCell.description: One cell of a workbook sheet. value is the raw value by type (a number for number and date - a date stays its serial number -, the text of a text or error cell, a boolean; null for empty); text is what Excel displays at unlimited width, drawn by Singularity's one number formatter.

fill.description: A "*x" repeat fill in the number format: before hugs the cell's left edge, after its right edge.

formula.description: With its leading "="; a shared formula translated to this cell.

previousText.description: What a changed cell showed in comparedToVersion; "" otherwise.

DocumentViewSheetCellStyle.description: A cell's own look, as the workbook declares it. Colours are "RRGGBB" with theme colours and tints resolved; "" is the workbook's default text colour, no fill, or a colour that does not resolve. Border edges carry the workbook's own line style name, "" for none.

fillColor.description: A solid pattern's fgColor; "" for none or any other pattern.

fontSizePoints.description: null where the size is the workbook's default.

AccountState.description: Who is signed in to Legal Machines on this computer. Identifiers and display names only: never a password, a code or a session token. organisationEmail is the firm's own email every seat signs in with, as typed here; role says whether the seat is the firm's administrator's or a colleague's; hasDownloadSession says whether this computer holds its native-only model download session.

AccountSignInResult.description: What a sign-in step came to. signed_in: the account and this computer's download session are kept; a missing protection model downloads at once only when onboarding is complete and protection is on, and otherwise when the member asks. two_factor_required: send the code with account.verifyTwoFactor and challengeId. email_verification_required: the organisation's email must be confirmed first; nothing was kept. awaiting_approval: Legal Machines has not approved the new organisation yet; nothing was kept, and maskedEmail is where it writes once it does. setup_required: a new organisation whose setup is not finished goes on with setup (two_factor); the token that opens it stays native. method, with two_factor_required: authenticator when the seat's authenticator app shows the code (a recovery code stands in once), email when a code was mailed. saved_password_refused: a sign-in asked with savedPassword, and the password this computer kept for the seat was refused by Legal Machines or is no longer kept; it is forgotten, nothing was kept, and the page asks for the password.

organisationId.description: Set by account.signInWithEmail: the organisation the password opened.

seatId.description: Set by account.signInWithEmail: the seat the password opened, which account.verifyTwoFactor takes.

usedRecoveryCode.description: Set by account.verifyTwoFactor when the second step was a recovery code: the page asks for a new authenticator app.

recoveryCodesLeft.description: With usedRecoveryCode: how many recovery codes are left unused.

onboardedHere.description: With signed_in: whether this seat finished onboarding on this computer before; then onboarding stands complete again, and the page goes straight back to work.

twoFactorSetup.description: "required": a colleague's seat with no authenticator yet sets one up before it works.

AccountLookup.description: Whether Legal Machines knows an organisation by this email, the one every seat of the firm signs in with.

AccountAgreements.description: The person's own acceptance of each legal document, never assumed: the Software Licence and Terms of Use, the Privacy Notice, consent to the processing of personal data, authority to act for the organisation, and that its email is a shared mailbox, not a person's.

AccountRegistration.description: A new organisation and its first seat. A code went to maskedEmail; account.confirmEmail takes it. Nothing is kept on this computer until the organisation signs in.

AccountEmailConfirmation.description: What confirming the organisation's email came to: awaiting_approval until Legal Machines approves it, or active. setup, for a new organisation created by account.create: what its setup sets first, password or two_factor; the token that opens it stays native.

AccountCodeSent.description: A new code went to the email that waits to be confirmed.

firmCopy.description: Held here from the firm's record: changed on the computer that runs it.

viewer.description: Who is looking and what they may do, the same viewer organisation.get holds.

firstSeenAt.description: When their computer first joined the Matter; empty when its record does not say.

invited.description: Given the Matter from this computer by choosing them, with no record of their own in it yet.

about.description: What they would have the firm know of them, in their own words, at most 600 characters; empty when they said nothing.

archived.description: Archived by the firm: their seat closed, their history kept.

removed.description: Removed from the firm: named only where they wrote.

PrivacyCoverage.description: The privacy overview's counts and Papinian Guard's state, without what left this device: nothing of the routing log is read.

ChatLatestMessage.description: A thread's latest message as a list of Matters shows it: who wrote it and its words in one line of at most 160 letters, without source markers. A person's message names their actor id and name, an AI colleague's its agent id and name; a model's answer to a person's own request names no one.

ChatReadMarks.description: What the member at this computer has read of each conversation: by its chat's id, the time of the latest message seen there. Kept on this computer with the member's preferences, never in a Matter's folder.

FirmColleagueList.description: The firm's colleagues other computers of the firm run.

FirmColleague.description: A colleague of the firm that another of the firm's computers runs, as the firm's record holds it: who it is, its office, how it works and what it does, its model, its status and who answers for it.

description.description: What the Matter is and for whom, as New Matter asked it; empty when nothing was said. Read on every change, so an edit on another computer shows here.

archivedAt.description: When it was archived; empty while it is open.

archivedBy.description: Who archived it, by actor id; empty while it is open.

DocumentChangeStep.description: One step of a change to a document, as the change describes it (Document/Types/DocumentChangeDescription.hpp document_change_step_json): a key it has no value for is left out.

ProjectChatEntry.description: A chat as a Project lists it (MatterBridge.cpp serialize). Its draft, working document and agent are read with chat.list (ProjectChat).

outcome.description: What the result is for the lawyer: completed, partial, blocked, unchanged or failed; empty until handed in.

label.description: What the colleague calls the document when it speaks of it: "the NDA".

AssignmentDecision.description: What only the lawyer can decide in an assignment: the question, why it matters, where, the options with the colleague's recommendation first, and whether the next step waits on it.

reasoning.description: Why the colleague recommends its first option, in a sentence; shown once, with that option. Empty when none.

ackMessageId.description: The colleague's reply that took the work up, which the assignment's card stands under.

AssignmentDecisionAnswer.description: The assignment once the lawyer answered one of its decisions, and the message that said it to the colleague.

AccountApprovalState.description: Whether Legal Machines approved the organisation that waits for it.

AccountSetupStep.description: A new organisation's setup goes on: two_factor is next.

AccountTwoFactorKey.description: The key an authenticator app takes for a new organisation's administrator: secret to type by hand, uri (otpauth://totp/...) to scan as a QR code.

AccountTwoFactorOn.description: Two-factor authentication is on and the setup is over: the organisation is active (or, from an older service, waits for Legal Machines' approval), and recoveryCodes are shown this once; they stay in memory here for account.saveRecoveryCodes and account.printRecoveryCodes while the app runs. signedIn, when the call gave seatId and password and the service gave its verified sign-in: the administrator is signed in here at once, as account.verifyTwoFactor would answer, and no code is asked again; the password is used for this call only.

AccountRecoveryCodesSaved.description: Whether the recovery codes were written to a file the person chose; false when they cancelled the Save dialog.

AccountRecoveryCodesPrinted.description: Whether the recovery codes' page to print was opened, with its print dialog, in the system's browser.

personActorId.description: The member the note is kept for, by their seat; the window says their name as it is now.

saidByActorId.description: Who said it, by their seat.

FirmSeat.description: A seat of the firm: a login of the firm's with no person in it, its id drawn by Legal Machines from a random set; the firm's administrator's or a colleague's.

twoFactor.description: Whether it signs in with an authenticator's code.

FirmSeatList.description: The firm's seats, the administrator's first, and the firm's email they all sign in with, when this computer knows it.

FirmSeatMade.description: A colleague's seat the administrator made: its id, which the colleague signs in with together with the firm's email and the password the administrator set.

FirmSeatChanged.description: A colleague's seat has a new password; its computers were signed out.

FirmSeatRemoved.description: A colleague's seat is gone, with its computers' sessions.

SeatProfile.description: Who sits in one of the firm's seats, as the firm's own record says: their name, their role on the firm's scale, their own title, their practice and their photo. Kept between the firm's computers, never at Legal Machines.

about.description: What they would have the firm know of them, in their own words, at most 600 characters; empty when they said nothing.

state.description: Where the colleague stands with the firm: empty at work, archived or removed.

SeatProfileList.description: Every seat the firm's record says who sits in.

FirmComputer.description: One of the firm's computers as this computer sees it: its seat, its device, its device key's code and whether a lawyer here checked it by the number both computers show. Public keys only, never a name.

FirmComputerList.description: The firm's computers as last read from Legal Machines, and the computers that began a check with this one.

ComputerCheck.description: A check of one of the firm's computers: waiting for the other computer, ready with the eight digits both show, failed with words for the lawyer, or none under way.

MatterGiven.description: A Matter given to a lawyer of the firm by choosing them; `reaches` says whether they have a computer a lawyer here checked, which the offer reaches now.

MatterOffer.description: A Matter a lawyer of the firm gave this member, from a computer a lawyer here checked, not yet answered.

MatterOfferList.description: The Matters offered to this member that wait for their answer.

ChosenFolder.description: The folder a lawyer chose for a new Matter, in the system's dialog: its path, its name, whether it holds a Matter already and which, and the token project.create takes it by - the path itself is never written back by the window.

HeldMatter.description: The Matter a chosen folder holds already, and where it stands on this computer: trashed in the Trash, listed among the Matters, or away - deleted from this computer or never opened here.

ColleagueDeleted.description: An AI colleague the firm let go: gone from every computer, its words kept where it wrote them.

OwnSeat.description: This computer's own seat: its id, its role, whether two-step sign-in is on and, where Legal Machines says it, how many of its recovery codes are left unused, whether its firm is one of Legal Machines' design partners, whose seats report problems and share work logs, whether this computer keeps and offers work logs (a design partner's seat on a build that holds Legal Machines' keys for them), and the version of the Diagnostics Consent this seat accepted, or null.

OwnTwoFactorKey.description: The key an authenticator app takes, typed or scanned from its otpauth link.

OwnTwoFactorOn.description: Two-step sign-in on, with the ten recovery codes, shown once.

SeatTwoFactorReset.description: A colleague's two-step sign-in turned off; they set it again at their next sign-in.

RecoveryRequested.description: A recovery code mailed to the firm's confirmed email, when it is one.

LetterReplyOpened.description: A reply to a filed letter opened in the member's mail app, never sent; with attachmentDocumentIds it opens as an unsent email carrying those documents. carriesText false when the text was too long for a mail link.

SeatPasswordStore.description: Where this computer can keep a seat's password at the member's choice: windows, the user's Credential Manager, on this computer only; null where it keeps none (macOS and Linux for now), and the page offers none.

SavedSeatPassword.description: Whether this computer keeps a password for the seat, named by the firm's email and the seat as the sign-in names it (none for the administrator's). Never the password: a sign-in uses it with savedPassword.

SeatPasswordSaved.description: Whether the password was kept: only for the seat that signed in on this computer in the last ten minutes, and only the very password it signed in with.

SeatPasswordForgotten.description: Whether a kept password was forgotten; false when none was kept.

ProblemPicture.description: A screenshot a Debug build's problem report carries: its file name and its PNG, JPEG or WebP bytes in base64.

ProblemReported.description: A problem report made a card of its version's board, by its number there.

WorkLogPreview.description: What a design partner's member sees before sending a chat's work log: the model calls this computer keeps for it, how many went under client data protection, without it or failed, from when to when, how many bytes, and whether it can be sent now, with why not in words.

WorkLogMessage.description: One message of the conversation as the member's page shows it, sent inside the sealed work log.

WorkLogShared.description: A work log sealed to Legal Machines' keys and taken by its intake: the SHA-256 of what was sealed, as the intake logged it, how many of Legal Machines' addresses it went to, and its size sealed.

UsageConfirmCostsResult.description: What usage.confirmCosts did: the OpenRouter calls of the Matter in the period whose cost OpenRouter's own record now confirms, those it does not have yet, and whether Legal Machines timestamped this computer's work record.
